about: How much each body weighs what a plan does when it chooses among printed plans. A commission set up by law to be independent weighs equal population and the Voting Rights Act and ignores party seats; a legislature weighs seats for its majority party and keeping its members apart, and avoids a plan a court would strike. Weights are TUNABLE: a score of the plan's measured facts, checked in tests against the choices each body should make, never a roll.

drawerSeats.source: An independent commission is barred by its charter from favoring a party or incumbent (e.g. Cal. Const. art. XXI, sec. 2(e); Ariz. Const. art. 4, pt. 2, sec. 1(14)).

limitBreach.source: A plan over the level's population limit is not drawn: every body avoids it unless nothing else is left.
